correctness.rationale: For each new three-support vertex the old-vertex link admits explicit domination reductions to a line-graph clique complex of K3 joined to a+1 isolated vertices, a wedge of a+1 two-spheres. The previously built complex remains two-connected so attaching cones adds (a+1) three-spheres; summing yields C(n+1,4). Coordinate projections supply independent signed three-coordinate sphere classes Λ³Qⁿ. The entire 15-vertex four-coordinate complex is exhaustively enumerated, with orientation-correct signed Lefschetz values (5,-3,1,2,-1) for S4; subtraction shows the quotient sign line. Independent four-subset projections yield Λ⁴Qⁿ as quotient, and Maschke splitting gives the claimed representation. The packaged standard-library program enumerates all simplices and coordinate permutations for n=3..6 and explicitly tests link reductions for n=3..7. Finite tests do not replace the uniform proof; only the n=4 finite Lefschetz certificate is a critical finite lemma.

The examined 2021 paper covers the link mechanism but not equivariance; 2026 full-cube equivariance does not compute sublevel homology; 2024 facet and 2026 function-Rips results do not determine this module. value.rationale: The recent function-Rips construction singles out natural sublevel complexes whose coordinate permutation symmetries survive although full-cube translations do not. The complete character across all dimensions n≥3, including the nontrivial additional Λ⁴ permutation module, is not determined by the known nonequivariant Betti number C(n+1,4), and gives a structural and computable invariant for a natural entire family rather than a finite arbitrary table. It is explicitly limited to one cutoff and rational coefficients.
